findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed steel wool and wet paper towels in the basin of the hand washing sink in the cold room. CORRECTED- items were removed. Hand washing sinks are not to be used for any other purpose than hand washing, so as not to deter frequent hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a multipurpose scraper in the basin of the hand washing sink behind the rotisserie chickens in hot holding. CORRECTED- the utensil was removed from the sink. Dishes and other food contact surfaces should go directly to the three part sink after use to be properly washed-rinsed-sanitized. Hand washing sinks are not to be used for any other purpose than hand washing, so as not to deter frequent hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed sanitizer bottles in the HMS room to contain a low concentration of sanitizer for food contact surfaces (100 ppm). CORRECTED- bottles were remade, and observed to be at an acceptable concentration. Ensure sanitizer used for food contact surfaces is made and tested at a frequency to obtain the approved concentration as recommended by the manufacturer’s label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed worn out caulking behind wash section of triple sink in HMS room. Discussed with PIC and he put in a repair order to have the caulking replaced. Physical facilities should be maintained in good repair. Re-caulk sink by next routine inspection. [C]
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.comment: A scraper was observed in the basin of one of the meat room handwashing sinks. CORRECTED- PIC removed the tool from the sink. Ensure handsinks are only used for handwashing, no other purpose. Keep handsinks clear to facilitate frequent handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The sanitizer spray bottle in the HMS cold room was observed with 100ppm quat. CORRECTED- The spray bottle was emptied and refilled from the HMS wall mounted dispenser. Sanitizer was then observed at 300ppm quat. Ensure sanitizers are prepared to correct concentration, and that solutions are remade regularly as needed.
4-501.114: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 200-400 ppm concentration, according to manufacturer’s label. [P]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: The sanitizer spray bottle in the meat cold room was empty. Upon inspector’s request, the sanitizer bottle was filled from the meat room’s wall-mounted sanitizer dispenser. Sanitizer was observed with a concentration of 300ppm quat. Ensure sanitizer is prepared prior to engaging in any food prep.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11 (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [C]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Sliced Tuscan-style turkey breast packages in the deli cooler were observed at 52F (probed). CORRECTED- Two boxes were voluntarily discarded. The unit was entering a defrost cycle. Other foods in the cooler were 43F to 39F. Monitor cooler temperatures and review stocking practices with staff to avoid overfilling coolers or stocking past the fill-lines.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Packages of ribs in the refrigerated prep room were observed with surface temperatures at 77F-79F. Internal temperature of ribs was observed at 78F and 81F with facility and inspector’s probe thermometers. Ribs are a pre-cooked frozen product that typically thaw overnight in the walk-in cooler prior to cooking the next operating day. Ribs were not pulled the day prior for thawing in the cooler. HMS staff were asked to thaw ribs under cold running water. Exact timeframe and water temperature used to thaw ribs prior to storage in refrigerated room were unknown. Management chose to discard product. Ensure proper thawing of ribs and proper cold holding if product will not be immediately cooked for service.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Sanitizer solutions were not available for use in the rotisserie chicken or HMS prep areas. Spray bottles in both areas were empty. Quat solutions were provided in spray bottles during inspection. Employee working rotisserie chicken prep noted they sometimes use a sani-bucket rather than spray bottle. Whether using a sani-bucket or spray bottle, solutions need to be prepared and available for use prior to beginning prep and food handling in the designated areas. 
**See general comments for additional information**
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towels were not available at the handwashing sink in the refrigerated prep room. Paper towels were provided during inspection.
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Spray bottles at front rotisserie area and in refrigerated prep room were observed at 100ppm quat. Fresh solutions were provided at 200ppm. Ensure spray bottles of sanitizer are checked with test strips to verify concentration and refreshed as needed prior to concentration becoming weak and ineffective.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Washing fruits and vegetables
findings.citation_text:
3-302.15 Vegetable wash connected to dispenser in HMS prep area was not at proper concentration. The test strip changed to a color outside of the acceptable dilution range for proper ppm. Packets of Kay Vegi Wash were available and will be used until dispenser is repaired and functioning properly. A call for service was made during the inspection. ** See general comments for additional information**
Chemicals used in the washing or to assist in the peeling of fruits and vegetables, for the washing of raw, whole fruits and vegetables shall be used in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-703.11 Serving spoon was observed resting on top of a cutting board in the sanitize compartment at the 3 part sink in HMS/rotisserie area. Spoon was not properly submerged to allow for proper sanitization of all surfaces. Spoon and cutting board were pushed down into the sanitizer solution to allow for proper sanitization of all surfaces. Proper immersion and contact time during ware washing were discussed.
After being cleaned, equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in chemical manual operations, including the application of sanitizing chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114 in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions. Contact time shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use instructions by providing at least 30 seconds for quaternary ammonia chemical sanitizing solutions.

findings.title: Washing fruits and vegetables
findings.citation_text:
3-302.15 Jug of antimicrobial fruit and vegetable treatment was empty at the 3 part sink in HMS/rotisserie area. An employee that works HMS confirmed the product is used by HMS staff when preparing meals that contain a fresh fruit or vegetable ingredient. Lead over HMS/rotisserie stated another jug was currently unavailable, but an order was placed for the product during the inspection. Packets of Kay Vegi Wash were provided for use until the order is received. Ensure staff know where test strips are for preparation of the Vegi Wash, which requires the use of chlorine test strips. Lactic acid test strips are required for the other product that has been ordered. An order was also placed to purchase new lactic acid test strips as the ones available appeared to be water damaged. 
Chemicals used in the washing or to assist in the peeling of fruits and vegetables, for the washing of raw, whole fruits and vegetables shall be used in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 Left side of the 3 part sink in HMS/rotisserie was observed pulling away from the wall. Mold accumulation was observed on the wall just above the backsplash of the 3 part sink. Clean the wall above the 3 part sink, and re-seal the 3 part sink to the wall.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.citation_text:
6-501.18 Mold buildup was observed in the basin and drain of the handsink in the refrigerated prep room. The drain in the handsink at the rotisserie chicken area was also soiled with buildup. Cleaning of handsinks and related fixtures was discussed. 
Plumbing fixtures such as handsinks shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.15 Employee that just washed a knife at the 3 part sink was observed rinsing his hands with the sprayer prior to continuing with the next task. Employee noted he was going to check inventory and always washes his hands prior to engaging in food handling. Employee was advised it is a bad practice to rinse hands at the 3 part sink regardless of the next task and to always properly wash hands at a designated handsink. Employee stated he understood and was observed properly washing hands at the handsink for the remainder of the inspection. 

Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food preparation or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 750-140b Observed unlabeled rack of cooling chicken. Some of the cooled foods are probed at 33F and some probed at 77-90F. Without labeling present, the actual start time of two separate cooling incidents was unable to be determined.  The chicken was discarded during the inspection. Discussed time labeling for cooling products. Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-530a Observed employee chewing gum during food preparation. Discussed increased production of saliva. Discarded gum. Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: No thermometer in hot holding. 750.150(a) All hot units that contain potentially hazardous foods shall contain  a conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F Provide thermometer.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: Floors along cove around hand sink and behind coat cabinet are soiled. 750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: Wall under hose caddy has a hole. 750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Seal hole. Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: The floor at the drain under the rotisserie has chipped flooring around the edge. 700-1200a Floors shall be smooth, durable and maintained in good repair. Repair floor material to be smooth and easily cleansable.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: The hand sink in rotisserie is no longer sealed to the wall. 750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings. Replace caulk seal to make sure that sink is sealed to the wall.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment: 750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination. In use aprons, lab coats, and hair nets were stored on the non-food table where chickens are boxed. Provide and Use proper storage for in use uniforms.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text: 750.140  There was no thermometer in the hot display case.  A thermometer was placed in the case to correct.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed a case of single service containers stored on the floor in the prep-cooking area of the deli. (corrected)
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.
